clue.text: Tin — usual material for construction of submarine?

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so these letters are assembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether tin is the normal stuff to build a submarine from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction of' rearranges TIN and USUAL. The question mark flags that the definition is a famous example: Jules Verne's fictional submarine and the first nuclear submarine both bore this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo's vessel and the US Navy's first nuclear-powered boat were both named after the sea creature.

clue.text: Extra given by wealthy chap to everyone

parts.note: a nob is a rich or upper-class person
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A rich man hands out a bonus to all.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a no-ball is an illegal delivery that gives the batting side a run, one of the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a no-ball adds a penalty run to the score, counted among the extras.

clue.text: Intruder is initially not very interested in football team

definitions.note: a noun standing for an adjective: an intruder is one who is not invited

indicators.note: in places the initials inside the team name

parts.note: United is the name of many football teams, Manchester United above all

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A gatecrasher is not much interested in his football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes INVI from 'is not very interested'; 'in' places it inside UNITED.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is by nature someone unasked, so the adjective describes him; the clue loosely swaps noun for adjective.

clue.text: I had one of my ears half-baked

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
I is the Roman numeral for one
otic is the medical adjective meaning relating to the ear

explanation.surface: Someone complains that one ear of theirs is only partly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: OTIC is a medical word meaning 'of the ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-baked means foolish or ill-thought-out, matching an adjective for stupid behaviour.

clue.text: Escort drug addict found in possession of heroin

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the addict contains the drug's letter

parts.note: a user is someone who takes drugs habitually
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A guard accompanies an addict caught with heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in possession of' puts H inside USER.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, so as a verb or noun it means to escort or an escort.

clue.text: Doctors about to adopt Chinese principle for collection of information

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the doctors take the Chinese principle inside them
about signals turning the doctors' letters back to front

parts.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors
yin is the passive female principle of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: Medical people about to embrace a Chinese idea in order to gather data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the doctors back to front before 'to adopt' takes in the Chinese principle; the definition is the long phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is covert gathering of intelligence, a form of collecting information.

clue.text: He painted a young chicken

definitions.meaning: Nicolas ... was a French classical painter of the seventeenth century
a chicken killed young for eating

explanation.definitionFit: The French painter's surname is also the culinary word for a small young chicken.

clue.text: I am left running out of navy dye

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: running out of means leaving, so the letter departs from the colour

parts.note: navy blue is a dark shade of blue

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a dark blue colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' gives L, and 'running out of' drops it from the colour, leaving BUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or stain with colour, so it can mean to dye.

clue.text: Jack, perhaps, among good cards, is welcome

indicators.note: among puts one piece inside the others

parts.note: a hand is the set of cards a player holds
Jack is an example of a boy's name, so a lad

explanation.surface: A card player is pleased when the jack turns up among strong cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like the playing card, but here it is just a boy's name, standing for any young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To glad-hand is to greet effusively, as a politician does, so it means to welcome.

clue.text: Share quarters and have a great laugh

definitions.meaning: to share a room or lodgings with someone
to bend over helplessly with laughter

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to share accommodation and to be convulsed with laughter.

clue.text: Anglo-American capital in Canadian province

parts.note: Anglo- means English or British
Columbia is the state capital of South Carolina

explanation.surface: An Anglo-American capital city located somewhere in a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'Anglo-American' reads as one word, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The westernmost province of Canada, with Vancouver and Victoria, carries this name.

clue.text: Composer carries books around, producing muscle

indicators.note: around signals turning the whole assembly back to front
carrying something means holding it within, so the composer contains the books

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible before the Gospels

explanation.surface: A composer lugging volumes about gives himself a pulled muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' builds ROTAVEL, and 'around' reads that whole thing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A levator is an anatomical term for any muscle that raises a body part, such as an eyelid.

clue.text: Ask to plant type of tree round the Home Counties?

indicators.note: round means the tree goes around the region's letters

parts.note: the beech is a kind of tree one might plant
SE, the South East of England, is where the Home Counties surrounding London lie

explanation.surface: A request to plant some kind of tree all around the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties encircling London, in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg or implore, a stronger synonym for asking.

clue.text: A docket's scrawled for fence

indicators.note: scrawled writing is messy, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone has hastily written a receipt for a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrawled' rearranges A DOCKETS, the S of docket's included.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a barrier or enclosure of upright stakes, a kind of defensive fence.

clue.text: Sir Anthony's rank

definitions.meaning: Sir Anthony ... is the irascible father in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals
rank as an adjective means utter or complete, as in a rank outsider

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Sheridan's character is also an adjective meaning total or out-and-out.

clue.text: At present batting, with success impossible

parts.note: now means at the present time
in cricket the batting side is in

explanation.surface: A cricketer currently at the crease with no chance of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where no outcome can be a victory, so success is out of reach.

clue.text: Tatum's tour de force?

parts.note: Art Tatum was a virtuoso American jazz pianist, so a masterpiece of his is a creation belonging to Art

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the pun on Art Tatum's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterly creation is a fine creative piece, and here literally one by a man named Art.

clue.text: Turkish soldier, we hear, is enlisted for middle of month

indicators.note: enlisted in place of the central letter, so a new piece replaces the month's middle U

parts.note: January is the first month of the year

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like IZ

explanation.surface: A Turkish soldier, reportedly, joins up in mid-January.
explanation.walkthrough: JANUARY's middle letter is U; 'we hear' turns IS into its sound IZ, which replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: Janizaries were the elite infantry of the Ottoman sultans, so a soldier of Turkey.

clue.text: Make sense of tot

definitions.meaning: to ... is to be logical or consistent, as in 'it doesn't ...'
to tot up is to total figures, to calculate a sum

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: being logically coherent, and totting numbers into a sum.

clue.text: Carrying boat overland from harbour, taking a long time

parts.note: a port is a harbour
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A boat is lugged overland from the harbour, a slow job.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is the carrying of a boat or goods over land between two navigable waters.

clue.text: Perhaps I could be turned to stone

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A speaker wonders whether they could be petrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be turned' rearranges PERHAPS I; 'to' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious gemstone, usually blue, so it is a kind of stone.

clue.text: Henry and I getting message somewhere in Canada

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a fax is a message sent by telephone line

explanation.surface: Henry and I receive a communication somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Halifax is the capital of Nova Scotia, a city in Canada.

clue.text: Southern volunteers get nervous reaction still

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Southern reservists still twitch from nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless or unmoving, the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: Sovereign's not a risk

indicators.note: not means the letter A is excluded from the word

parts.note: imperial means belonging to an emperor or sovereign

explanation.surface: A claim that the monarch carries no danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A from IMPERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to put in danger, the same as to risk something as a verb.

clue.text: Geographical feature, one shown in map

indicators.note: shown in places the numeral inside the map

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram of an area
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A geographical feature, one shown on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' puts I inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is a broad flat expanse of land, a landform.

clue.text: Shout order to strike

definitions.meaning: a union calls out its members when it orders them to go on strike

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to yell and, in union language, to summon workers into an industrial walkout.

clue.text: Island where copper catches endless fish

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the copper's letters contain the fish

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the orfe is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: An island where a policeman catches a fish with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the chemical symbol; 'endless' cuts ORFE to ORF and 'catches' puts it inside CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Swimmers unimaginative, in reality

parts.note: the ASA is the Amateur Swimming Association, the governing body for British swimmers
matter-of-fact means prosaic and literal, lacking imagination

explanation.surface: Swimmers are a dull lot, if truth be told.
explanation.walkthrough: The ASA was the governing body of swimming in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to introduce what is actually true, meaning in fact or in reality.

clue.text: American — one who's pulled?

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a US citizen
read literally, someone who has been yanked, with -ee as in employee

explanation.definitionFit: The nickname for a US citizen can be read as yank plus -ee, one on the receiving end of a tug.

clue.text: One cox quit after bungling, being chivalrous

indicators.note: bungling is botching, so the pieces come out muddled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rowing coxswain gives up after a mistake, behaving nobly.
explanation.walkthrough: A cox steers a rowing boat, which gives the surface its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Quixotic, from Don Quixote, means idealistically gallant in a romantic, impractical way.
